portfolio.title: Portfolio Agent Platform
portfolio.description: A recruiter-facing agent with public MCP and GraphQL context, bounded tools, and reviewed contact actions.
portfolio.description_detail: Problem: make professional experience useful to recruiters and their agents. Approach: one approved content source feeds the website, résumé, MCP, GraphQL and grounded agent tools. Tradeoff: keep the public agent narrowly scoped, with signed access, durable usage budgets and reviewed contact actions instead of general execution. Verification: automated backend, frontend and browser checks plus deployment probes. Limitations: model answers can be mistaken; no calendar booking or arbitrary code execution.
portfolio.resume_description: Built this portfolio with FastAPI and React, deployed on Google Cloud Run.
portfolio.contribution: Designed and built the agent, public context APIs, contact workflow and deployment checks.
portfolio.evidence: Public source, working agent, read-only APIs, and automated unit/browser checks.
portfolio.maturity_note: Live on Cloud Run. Durable admission and contact delivery verified against release a0844ab on October 8, 2026; model answers still require judgment.

case_study.problem: Make professional experience easy for recruiters and their agents to inspect, while keeping model usage and contact actions bounded.
case_study.role: Designed and built the portfolio, agent context interfaces, contact workflow and release checks.
constraints: Public read-only context must remain separate from actions that send a message.
Multiple service instances must share inference limits.
Visitors need useful access without unrestricted model spending.
case_study.architecture: React and TypeScript present the portfolio and agent workspace. FastAPI serves approved JSON content through the website, MCP and GraphQL, and runs the grounded agent workflow. Supabase PostgreSQL stores shared access and inference accounting. Confirmed contact actions use the delivery service; the application is packaged for Cloud Run.

decisions.decision: Derive website and agent interfaces from shared approved content.
decisions.tradeoff: Consistency and inspectability take priority over unrestricted retrieval. Content still needs human maintenance.

decisions.decision: Reserve inference tokens atomically before provider execution.
decisions.tradeoff: A failed accounting service denies new inference; missing usage remains charged conservatively.

decisions.decision: Require visitor review and validated identity fields for contact actions.
decisions.tradeoff: An extra confirmation step reduces accidental sends and separates model suggestions from visitor intent.

challenges.challenge: Keep public discovery useful without exposing action-capable tools.
challenges.resolution: Publish read-only MCP and bounded GraphQL separately from confirmed agent actions.

challenges.challenge: Prevent instance restarts or concurrent replicas from resetting spending controls.
challenges.resolution: Use durable reservation and settlement records with shared database limits.

outcomes.statement: The public portfolio exposes the same professional context through human-facing pages and machine-readable interfaces.
The deployed source includes regression tests for reservation denial, unavailable accounting and conservative usage settlement.

limitations: Calendar booking and arbitrary code execution are unavailable.
Automated checks do not prove immunity to every abuse pattern.
Local and release checks cover defined journeys, not every model response or workload.

pointup.title: PointUp
pointup.description: A loyalty portfolio with trip goals, qualified redemption estimates and reviewable agent proposals across web, MCP and browser-extension workflows.
pointup.description_detail: PointUp organizes loyalty memberships, balances, expiry context and trip goals. Its public source defines a framework-independent TypeScript domain core shared by the Next.js web app, workers, MCP, typed API clients and browser extension. Supported balance capture requires consent; transfer and redemption values are qualified estimates, not bookable prices. The modern source does not by itself establish completion of the legacy application’s data migration.
pointup.resume_description: Built a loyalty portfolio with shared TypeScript workflows for web, agents and consented browser capture.
pointup.contribution: Developed the loyalty portfolio and shared domain workflows for web and agent surfaces.
pointup.evidence: Public source and architecture documentation; the PointUp public page was reachable on October 8, 2026.
pointup.maturity_note: Public product surface; provider sync, award data and legacy migration have separate qualification gates.

case_study.problem: Loyalty balances and trip goals are scattered across programs, while automated collection and redemption estimates have different trust requirements.
case_study.role: Developed PointUp’s product and shared application workflows, evolving the earlier PointBot experiment.
constraints: Reference coverage does not imply automatic access to every loyalty program.
Visitors must review agent-proposed changes before they affect their portfolio.
Legacy application data needs a separately accepted migration.
case_study.architecture: A TypeScript monorepo separates framework-independent domain and application logic from infrastructure adapters. Next.js and React provide the web surface; Drizzle and PostgreSQL persist portfolio data, with Clerk identity. Shared contracts support workers, MCP, typed API clients and the Chrome extension.

decisions.decision: Share domain use cases across web, workers and agent interfaces.
decisions.tradeoff: Adapter contracts require maintenance, but business rules do not need separate implementations for each surface.

decisions.decision: Present redemption values as qualified estimates and keep agent changes reviewable.
decisions.tradeoff: The product avoids promising automatic access or bookable prices that available sources cannot establish.

challenges.challenge: Support multiple interaction surfaces without giving each a different balance or goal model.
challenges.resolution: Use shared contracts and domain/application boundaries with surface-specific adapters.

challenges.challenge: Distinguish a convincing local demo from a working provider integration.
challenges.resolution: Document seeded local data, simulated sync and configured-provider acceptance separately.

outcomes.statement: The public repository contains the modern PointUp application and documents its web, worker, MCP and extension boundaries.
A public PointUp product page is available; this is not proof of every authenticated or provider-dependent workflow.

limitations: Automatic sync depends on an authorized, configured adapter.
Redemption estimates are not live award inventory or bookable prices.
Source and CI evidence do not certify completion of the legacy data migration.

data_playground.title: Data Playground
data_playground.description: A reproducible synthetic commerce lab for event validation, SQL metrics, dependency DAGs, graphs and vector similarity.
data_playground.description_detail: Built a reproducible synthetic commerce pipeline with seeded event generation, deduplication, schema and lifecycle checks, and SQL analytics. Explore acquisition and retention scenarios, inspect quarantined records, and trace conversion, collected revenue, and cohort retention to the queries that compute them. The public React lab serves generated Python runs without a database; a bounded FastAPI service supports custom simulations when configured. A separate synthetic commerce dataset connects products, customers, and purchases in a relationship graph and explains cosine similarity over handcrafted product feature vectors. An engineering workbench exposes executable dependency DAGs, retry and failure traces, model grains and contracts, and architecture decisions grounded in the implementation. The original PostgreSQL and Streamlit experiment remains in the source repository.
data_playground.contribution: Built the deterministic Python lab and its interactive portfolio explorer.
data_playground.evidence: Public engine, architecture documentation and reproducible catalogue contract.
data_playground.maturity_note: Synthetic educational lab; no customer data or verified standalone hosted service.

case_study.problem: Make data-pipeline behavior and business metrics explainable through reproducible examples rather than opaque dashboard numbers.
case_study.role: Built the synthetic commerce engine, validation and analytics workflow, and the portfolio’s interactive explorer.
constraints: All examples must use synthetic data.
The same configuration, scenario and engine version must reproduce the same result.
Missing observation windows must not be reported as zero retention.
case_study.architecture: The Python repository owns event simulation, validation, analytics, the CLI, an optional FastAPI service and a reproducible catalogue export. The portfolio repository owns the React explorer. Separate graph/vector examples and executable DAG demonstrations expose their own synthetic inputs and execution boundaries; the supported lab requires no external database or credentials.

decisions.decision: Use deterministic generation and an exported catalogue shared with the UI.
decisions.tradeoff: Reproducibility and inspection come before live-data realism.

decisions.decision: Represent money as integer cents and unobserved retention ages as null.
decisions.tradeoff: More explicit metric semantics prevent convenient but misleading comparisons.

decisions.decision: Keep the supported lab separate from the legacy PostgreSQL experiment.
decisions.tradeoff: The self-contained lab is easier to reproduce but does not demonstrate a running production data warehouse.

challenges.challenge: Explain why a record or metric is wrong instead of silently accepting it.
challenges.resolution: Expose lifecycle checks, quarantined records and the SQL behind the resulting metrics.

challenges.challenge: Make orchestration behavior inspectable beyond a static diagram.
challenges.resolution: Provide executable DAG examples with callbacks, retry traces and blocked dependencies.

outcomes.statement: The public project documents reproducible catalogue exports and compares repeat exports in CI.
The architecture workbench exposes executable dependency, retry and failure behavior.

limitations: Handcrafted feature-vector similarity is not a trained recommendation system.
The legacy PostgreSQL services are not established as functional by the supported lab.

ai_billing.title: AI Thread Billing
ai_billing.description: A prototype for per-thread AI token metering and cost reporting through an event-driven billing pipeline.
ai_billing.description_detail: A React chat workspace connects to FastAPI over WebSocket with an HTTP send fallback. A separate collector, Kafka, Redis and SQLite support usage and billing events; Streamlit exposes cost analytics. The development workspace uses a seeded demo identity and has no authentication. Invoice creation exists in the backend but is unavailable in the React interface. The portfolio demo is a separate synthetic browser illustration; neither it nor the source establishes provider-backed billing acceptance.
ai_billing.resume_description: Built a prototype for per-thread AI usage metering and event-driven cost reporting.
ai_billing.contribution: Built the chat-usage metering prototype and event/billing workflow.
ai_billing.evidence: Public README, system/data-model diagrams and implementation documentation.
ai_billing.maturity_note: Unauthenticated development prototype; no verified standalone hosted deployment.

super_teacher.title: Super Teacher
super_teacher.description: A classroom copilot that answers 'who needs me today, and why?' with a ranked needs-attention list, a gradebook, attendance, and a streaming Claude assistant grounded in the class data.
super_teacher.description_detail: Super Teacher is a classroom copilot for teachers. A Today view ranks the students who need attention with plain-language reasons; a roster, gradebook, and one-tap attendance feed the same computed averages, trends, and risk, so every screen agrees. Reports cover per-assignment class statistics, a CSV gradebook export, and AI-drafted parent updates the teacher edits before sending. An Ask AI chat streams from Claude with tools that query the real roster data, and per-student insight cards fall back to rule-based text when no API key is set. Built with a FastAPI backend on SQLAlchemy 2 and SQLite with Alembic migrations, and a React and Vite front end.
super_teacher.resume_description: Built a classroom copilot with a streaming Claude assistant, prioritized student needs, a gradebook, and attendance.
super_teacher.contribution: Built a classroom copilot with a streaming Claude assistant, prioritized student needs, a gradebook, and attendance.
super_teacher.evidence: Public architecture, screenshot and deployment-status documentation; source features and live deployment are tracked separately.
super_teacher.maturity_note: Public source; the linked earlier deployment does not certify the current application.
